Compute the Taylor number for Taylor-Couette flow between concentric rotating cylinders, using the standard textbook definition: Ta = (4 · Ω² · R_m · d³) / ν², where Ω is the angular velocity of the inner cylinder (outer cylinder stationary), R_m = (R_in + R_out)/2 is the mean cylinder radius, d = R_out − R_in is the radial gap width, and ν = μ/ρ is the kinematic viscosity of the working fluid.
Use the given geometry: R_in = 50 mm = 0.050 m, R_out = 52 mm = 0.052 m, so d = 0.002 m and R_m = 0.051 m.
Use the given rotation: only the inner cylinder spins at 100 rpm, giving Ω = 100 × 2π/60 ≈ 10.472 rad/s (do not rotate the outer cylinder).
Use the given fluid data: dynamic viscosity μ = 0.01 Pa·s, and adopt the recommended water-like density ρ ≈ 998 kg/m³ (purely for computing ν, since μ alone was specified), giving ν = μ/ρ ≈ 1.002 × 10⁻⁵ m²/s.
Evaluate the Taylor number using the locked-in convention: Ta = (4 × (10.472)² × 0.051 × (0.002)³) / (1.002 × 10⁻⁵)² ≈ (4 × 109.66 × 0.051 × 8 × 10⁻⁹) / (1.004 × 10⁻¹⁰) ≈ 1780 (dimensionless).
Report the result as Ta ≈ 1.78 × 10³ (using water-like density only to derive ν from the given μ).
State that the corresponding critical Taylor number for onset of Taylor vortices in the narrow-gap, fixed-outer-cylinder case is Ta_c ≈ 1708 (or ≈ 3390 in the radius-ratio-corrected form G^2 = Ta · (1 + d/2R_m)^(-4) ≈ 1708), and note that the calculated value is only marginally above the classical onset threshold, indicating the flow is essentially at the transition from laminar circular Couette flow to the first Taylor-vortex regime.
Provide units explicitly throughout (mm for lengths, rpm and rad/s for rotation, Pa·s for μ, kg/m³ for ρ, m²/s for ν, dimensionless for Ta).
